Alvin Toffler, author of influential 'Future Shock,' dead at 87

Toffler's long friendship with Newt Gingrich always puzzled me, given their diametrically opposed worldviews and Gingrich's reputation for being exceptionally nasty to those who didn't agree with him. But there was, for a short time, this peculiar love affair among corporate executives and Gingrich's Neo-Conservative movement with the language or terminology of Toffler's Third Wave series, even if it often seemed they didn't comprehend most of what it was about. There were CEOs in the '80s calling themselves 'Third Wave Executives' despite the fact that Toffler's vision of a Post-Industrial culture suggested an end to corporations and the Industrial Age paradigms as we knew them. It's also curious how the journalists pick up on his minor interest in space colonization when the core premise of most of his work was the idea of institutional, economic, industrial, and cultural 'demassification' as a consequence of advancing technology. His was a Libertarian-Socialist vision (in the original sense of the term 'libertarian', not the American version...) of future culture where the roles and powers of the state and finance industry were eroded and obsolesced by information technology.
